Dear Users,
We are committed to maintaining transparency about the development and creative processes behind our app. As part of this commitment, we would like to inform you that some of the artwork featured in our app has been partially generated using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools.
What This Means
The AI tools we use are employed to assist in creating and enhancing visual elements, such as concept art, textures, and design prototypes.
All AI-generated assets are thoroughly reviewed and, in most cases, modified by our team of designers and artists to ensure they align with our creative vision and meet our quality standards.
Why We Use AI
The integration of AI in our creative workflow allows us to:
Experiment with innovative visual styles and ideas.
Speed up the iteration process, enabling us to focus more on delivering a polished and engaging experience to you.
Expand our ability to create a wide range of high-quality assets efficiently.
Commitment to Creativity and Integrity
We want to emphasize that the use of AI is just one part of our creative process. The majority of the work is driven by the talent and expertise of our dedicated team of artists and developers. Additionally, we ensure that all AI-generated assets comply with intellectual property guidelines and ethical standards.

"Statement on Game Development Process:
During the early conceptual design and creative ideation phase of this game, we utilized AI technology as a supplementary tool to help us explore and validate various artistic styles and creative directions more efficiently. These AI-generated reference materials provided us with initial inspiration.
However, the core creative concepts, story writing, character design, and all final art assets presented in the game were personally conceived and carefully crafted by our creative team. Each game element has undergone multiple rounds of manual optimization and fine-tuning to ensure the best gaming experience.
AI was used solely as an assistive tool, while the final game content is the result of human craftsmanship. We remain committed to human-driven creation as our primary approach, dedicated to delivering a unique and meticulously polished gaming experience to our players."

AI was used to create all the visuals in the game. However, every illustration required manual reworking, whether through adjustments, graphic polishing, or integration into the game.
I understand that some may not appreciate this approach. Please know that my main goal has always been to create a fun and enjoyable game. I am a solo developer who left my job to dedicate 100% of my time to making video games.
To be honest, I don’t know how to model in 3D or illustrate in 2D, which is why I used AI as a support tool. I’m fully aware that AI can be seen as a sensitive topic, and that’s why I’ve been reworking the visuals as much as possible. My wish is also, if the game allows me the resources after release, to collaborate with a 2D artist to further enhance the visual identity.
Thank you sincerely for your understanding, and I truly hope you’ll enjoy playing Vampire Cat despite these choices. Your support means the world to me.

These models only process material you provide yourself, they do not invent content of their own, and the result stays inside your own lobby.

I put together the game's soundtrack using some AI tools to help with the initial ideas. They made it easy to quickly try out different melodies, beats, and sound effects, generating a bunch of variations in no time. From there, I went through everything by hand—tweaking, editing, and polishing until it all felt just right for the intense, quick matches. The AI was basically a time-saver that sped up brainstorming, but every final track was shaped and approved by me to nail that high-energy, competitive vibe. The procedure is as follows:
Based on detailed world-building settings, prompts are created and input into Dall-E 3 to generate images multiple times.
A single output image—or a combination of several output images—is then used as a reference sketch to create pixel art.
In addition, except for some parts, the map background images are also generated by creating prompts from the world-building settings and inputting them into Dall-E 3. The resulting images are then used as reference sketches to produce pixel art.
By following this method, while we leverage AI-generated images, the final designs are all completed as pixel art by human hands.

As the AI debate continues to evolve I feel the need to add nuance to this statement so players can make an informed decision whether or not to support human game developers.
I took 5 years of classes learning code and 3D to produce my game.  When the AI boom hit, Tobiano was already a functioning breeding and management simulator.  At my day job, we were encouraged to use AI for everything from image generation to writing emails.  I opposed the use of AI for creative aspects and human communication, but tested out chatbots for help with code.  Problems solved with AI include things like "how do i make the camera follow the player".  A lot of the problems ended up more convoluted by AI.
Most of the code written early in the game has gone through 2-3 iterations to simplify and be easier to work with and debug. For example, the riding lesson system was redone completely after the first 5 lessons were added, just to make the next 5 lessons easier for me to add.  Building a large and complex game requires understanding of code and the developer needs to know where to find every method, every variable.  There is an important distinction between "hey Claude, build me a horse game" and saving a couple hours writing a database. I've spent literally thousands of hours writing code for my passion project.
AI use in the game today consists of time-saving things like "add these markings to this list". AI can be useful for debugging, when the root of a problem can be a simple typo that is hard to spot. Bigger debugging problems always require a broader conceptual understanding of the way the game is set up and take human hours to solve. AI has not been used to create any 3D assets, textures, audio, or writing or translations in the game. I cannot guarantee that people I hire to do these tasks do not use AI, as these cooperations are based on trust.
My discord community see behind the scenes and know the care and work that goes into this game. As time goes on I take the gamble that my efforts will produce something that players can enjoy, knowing they are supporting human game developers.

The development of Fate War was transformed by AI—not as a replacement for artistry, but as a catalyst for it. By integrating AI technology into our pipeline, we streamlined art asset creation from initial concept to final implementation. This empowered rapid iteration, expanded stylistic exploration, and boosted production efficiency, freeing our artists to devote their expertise to creative vision rather than repetitive execution.
Yet technology alone cannot craft a living world. Every texture, every play of light, every meticulously placed detail was shaped by our art team's unwavering dedication. AI served as a brush, but the hand of the artist ensured each stroke resonated with purpose. The result is a fantasy realm where technology and human creativity unite—immersive, vibrant, and alive.

In our game development process, we have adopted AI technology to generate art content, mainly for the character portraits of esports players and illustrations in game events. We hope to provide players with richer and more diverse character portraits, but considering the economic, manpower, and time aspects, we find it difficult to afford a large amount of hand-drawn content. We have tried to separate parts such as the mouth, face, and nose, and then assemble them into 3D characters, but the effect was not satisfactory.
Therefore, we decided to try a new method: using AI to generate these contents. We used some of the content we had created before to train the AI model, allowing it to learn and understand the art style and requirements we want. Now, all the AI-generated character portraits and illustrations in the game are made by our trained model, and after completion, we also manually correct them.
We deeply understand that AI cannot replace the creativity and uniqueness of real artists. For this, we feel very sorry, but we also promise you that “Esports Godfather” is not a work without sincerity. We have spent a tremendous amount of time polishing innovative gameplay and various experience content. In these four and a half years, we have been committed to completing a work that satisfies everyone.
We hope you can understand our decision and continue to support our game. We will continue to work hard to provide you with a better gaming experience.

Some interface art (window and button icons, the game logo, the window header pattern and decorations such as pins, tape and clips) and the game's translations were created with the help of AI tools, then integrated by our team. The same art also appears on our store page and in our update announcements. Since version 3.1, the textures of the floors, walls, outdoor paths and grass in the game were also created with AI tools. The artwork of our Steam Trading Cards (the cards, badges, emoticons and profile backgrounds) was also created with AI tools. The game's 3D models, characters and gameplay were not made with AI, and no AI content is generated while you play.
